Independently recomputed finite chains, positive loops, stochastic rows and 2,560 representative Fourier eigenvalues (maximum observed modulus 0.9994626093913185<1); finite tests alone do not establish infinitely many modes or generic irrationality.

value.rationale: For the natural random Feres billiard on geodesic disks, the result pinpoints a mathematically surprising sharp qualitative contrast: a rational outgoing angle is spatially locked in a Euclidean disk but gains point-source weak spatial equidistribution at all but countably many curved radii in both constant-curvature signs, despite a finite nonmixing angular component. The nontrivial curvature-dependent geometric return-loop mechanism and all-mode nonlattice implication supply a useful exact boundary between spatial statistics and full-system mixing. It is motivated rather than a routine restatement of invariant-start mixing.

final_claim: For N≥7 and α=π/N, each 0<θ<α and either hyperbolic radius r>0 or spherical 0<r<π/2, all but countably many radii yield weak normalized-arclength convergence of the collision position law from any deterministic boundary location, with exponential decay of each fixed nonzero Fourier mode; for each fixed radius only countably many θ satisfy the displayed rational-phase resonance. Conversely Euclidean rational θ/π and rational α/π produce finite spatial subgroup trapping. No full-system mixing or TV limit follows.
